images.title: Divisor 4: only the last two digits decide
images.purpose: Shows the rule bench in its simplest state: with divisor 4, the thousands and hundreds blocks are shaded as multiples of 4 and only the last two digits are left to test.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no characters, no extra text. One row of three place value blocks across the centre with a divisor chip above.
images.exact_structure: Above the row, a small reddish purple (#CC79A7) chip holding divisor 4. Below it, three rounded blocks in one row joined by plus signs: 3 × 1000, 7 × 100 and 16. The first two blocks are filled teal (#0072B2) and share one brace underneath labelled multiples of 4. The third block, holding 16, is white with a thick amber (#E69F00) outline, and under it the label 16 = 4 × 4. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: 100 and 1000 are multiples of 4, so 3716 is divisible by 4 because its last two digits, 16, are.
